text: Under the Health Protection and Promotion Act and its regulations, Toronto Public Health (TPH) has environmental health responsibilities, including ensuring food safety, protecting the safety of water used for drinking and recreation, preventing the spread of infectious diseases transmitted by animals or insects (e.g. Rabies) and protecting the public from chemical and physical risks in the environment (e.g. heat relief network). Within TPH, these important components of public health practice are largely carried out by staff that are part of the Healthy Environments (HE) portfolio. This includes Public Health Inspectors (PHIs), Public Health and Preventive Medicine Physicians, Clerks, Quality Assurance Specialists and Tobacco Enforcement Officers.
